title: Your Brain Decides Seconds Before You Think You Do

scenes.text: Your brain makes your decisions up to seven seconds before you know.
In two thousand eight, scientists in Germany put people in a brain scanner and gave them one job: press a button with your left or right hand, whenever you feel like it.
The people felt they chose freely, at the last moment.
But a computer reading their brain activity could predict which hand they'd pick, up to seven seconds before they consciously decided.
The signal came from the front of the brain, which seems to prepare the choice long before you feel yourself making it.
So the moment you feel you decided may just be your brain telling you what it already did. Who's really in charge in there?

description:
Your brain makes your decisions up to seven seconds before you know.
In a 2008 study from the Max Planck Institute, published in Nature Neuroscience, volunteers in an fMRI scanner pressed a left or right button whenever they wanted. Activity in the frontopolar cortex predicted which button they would choose up to seven seconds before they reported deciding. Other brain areas predicted the timing of the movement up to five seconds ahead.
Who do you think is really in charge in there?
